about_company.about_short: NBFC providing supply chain finance to MSMEs and corporates in India.
about_company.about_long: SG Finserve is a non-deposit-taking NBFC registered with the RBI as an Investment and Credit Company and classified in the Middle Layer. It lends working capital to the dealers, distributors and vendors of large corporate anchors through dealer and vendor finance, invoice financing, factoring and TReDS, and in H1 FY27 it launched a loan-against-property product (starting in Delhi-NCR) and digital lending through a lending-service-provider partnership. Supply-chain finance was about two-thirds of its ₹5,694 Cr loan book at 30 September 2026. Income is almost all interest: ₹320.2 Cr of FY26's ₹333.7 Cr total income. Supply-chain loans carry stop-supply arrangements with the anchor, and the company has reported nil NPAs since lending began. It is part of the APL Apollo group but is not a subsidiary of APL Apollo Tubes: it is promoted by Rahul and Rohan Gupta, sons of Sanjay Gupta, whose promoter group held about 53% at March 2026.
about_company.business_intro: SG Finserve is an RBI-registered NBFC that finances the dealers, distributors and vendors of large companies against their invoices; if a borrower defaults, the anchor company stops supplying it. This supply-chain finance was about two-thirds of the ₹5,694 Cr loan book at September 2026; the rest is lending beyond the supply chain, such as loans against property and business loans. Interest is about 96% of income (FY26). It is promoted by Rahul and Rohan Gupta, sons of Sanjay Gupta, and is part of the APL Apollo group.

company_timeline.title: Incorporated as Moongipa Securities
company_timeline.detail: The company was incorporated in 1994 as Moongipa Securities Limited and received an RBI registration as a non-deposit-taking NBFC on 16 May 2018.

company_timeline.title: Starts supply-chain lending as SG Finserve
company_timeline.detail: Renamed SG Finserve in 2022, it began lending on 1 September 2022, at first entirely within the APL Apollo group's dealer and vendor network.

company_timeline.title: Gets RBI registration as a Type II NBFC
company_timeline.detail: The loan book was cut while the conversion was pending, from ₹1,891 Cr at December 2023 to ₹822 Cr at September 2024. The company called it a regulatory hurdle, regularised by the RBI in October 2024, and the book rebuilt to ₹2,246 Cr by March 2025.

business_facts.title: Loan book by region: North 44%, South 30%, West 23%, East 3%
business_facts.text: All lending is in India; the company has no overseas operations. By zone, the loan book at March 2025 was 44% North, 30% South, 23% West and 3% East. Later presentations do not repeat the split.

business_facts.title: Supply-chain finance is about two-thirds of the loan book
business_facts.text: Dealer, distributor and vendor finance, invoice financing, factoring and TReDS made up about two-thirds of the ₹5,694 Cr loan book at September 2026; the remaining third is lending beyond the supply chain. In December 2025 the issuer's own portfolio mix was 40% supply-chain finance within the APL Apollo group, 30% supply-chain finance outside it and 30% other lending. It worked with 52 anchor companies in July 2026 and added 14 new anchors in H1 FY27.

business_facts.title: Construction is the largest industry in the book, about 35% of AUM
business_facts.text: Construction was the largest industry in the book at about 35% of AUM in April 2026, with automotive second and mobile phones about 2%. Management says supply-chain finance suits a few industries: auto, steel, construction, white goods and IT peripherals.

business_facts.title: 92% of the loan book was secured at March 2026, up from 80%
business_facts.text: Secured loans were ₹3,628 Cr of the ₹3,936 Cr loan book at March 2026, against ₹1,807 Cr of ₹2,246 Cr a year earlier; security is a charge on the funded inventory and on the receivables from its sale. The same annual report also puts the secured share at 80% to 90% in its text and at 80-87% in its risk table.

business_facts.text: Loans are disbursed on a fully digital platform integrated with anchors' ERP systems. Since lending began it has financed more than 5.15 lakh invoices and disbursed over ₹65,000 Cr in total, including 1.65 lakh invoices and ₹25,368 Cr of gross disbursements in FY26.

business_facts.title: Board approves a GIFT City arm and two minority stakes
business_facts.text: On 16 October 2026 the board approved up to USD 5 million (about ₹48 Cr) for a wholly owned finance company in GIFT City, subject to regulatory approvals; buying 15.5% of Succesship Technologies for ₹4.65 Cr to build in-house AI and digital capabilities; and buying 24.5% of SG Enterprise Solutions, a new group shared-services company, from SG Green Buildings, a related party. Two wholly owned subsidiaries, SG Insurance Brokers and SG Alternative Investment Fund, were incorporated in the quarter and have not started operations.

what_changed.headline: APL Apollo group now about a quarter of the loan book
what_changed.text: Lending began in 2022 entirely within the APL Apollo group's dealer and vendor network. In December 2025 the group's ecosystem was still 40% of AUM, and in July 2026 management put it at about one-third. By September 2026 about 75% of the ₹5,694 Cr loan book sat outside the group, after 14 new anchor companies were added in H1 FY27 and more than 80% of the book's growth came from new customers.
